Relit billboards: one Kitchen, lit at runtime

A mirrored building sprite carries its painted light with it, so its sunny side swaps over and it stands out against its neighbours. Here the Kitchen is painted with even, shadowless light over a 3D blockout, then lit by the game's sun through the blockout's normal map. The mirror flips the picture and one sign of the normals, nothing else.

A look test. Nothing here runs in Unity.

The problem

Today's painted Kitchen and the same picture flipped. The paint carries its own light, so the flip moves the bright side from one wall to the other.

One building, under the game's sun

The same Kitchen four ways, each with its ground shadow. The baked sprite is the true 3D render with its light painted in; the relit sprite is the painting lit through the normal map. The ground shadow of each mirror is the shadow the mirrored building casts under the true sun.

Baked light

Stone walls facing screen right: 226 in the original, 112 in the mirror (mean luma), a ratio of 0.50.

Relit

Stone walls facing screen right: 183 in the original, 192 in the mirror, a ratio of 1.045. A true 3D mirror differs by as much (1.044): the two walls are not the same wall.

Six touching 3 × 3 plots, original and mirror in turn, under the game's sun.

At the phone's size

The relit street on a phone, 412 × 883 points, at the default zoom (24.4 points a unit) and the closest (63). The dark bands are the status bar with its camera hole, and the gesture bar.

Painted colour against blockout colour

The same relight over two colour layers: the painting, and the blockout's flat palette.

Painted

Blockout colour

Screen-right stone walls, mirror over original: 1.043, as in the painted pair (1.045). The front wall, with its recess and overhang, carries more occlusion than the door wall that takes its place in the mirror.

The sun through the day

The ground from above, north up; the line is the camera looking in from the south-west. A sun nearer the middle stands higher.

Relit

True 3D render

Style

Plain shading, or the same light through a ramp of three steps; and the painting's own fine detail read as relief over the blockout's normals, inside each face.

Stepping moves the building's tones by a mean of 19 of 255; the relief by 2.5, tilting the normals by a median 0.9° (95th percentile 11°), with 8.8 % of pixels moving by more than 8.

Relit against the true 3D render

The blockout's own colour relit, beside the true render under the same sun. Normals know which way a face points but not what stands between it and the sun: the roof's shadow in the recess, the chimneys' shadows on the roof. The occlusion term darkens corners the true render leaves lit.

Mean difference over the building: 11.2 of 255 for the original, 9.3 for the mirror; 32.9 % of the original's pixels differ by more than 16.

Chosen: C after its repair. C lines up with the blockout best of the three (overlap 0.984 after fitting, edges 2.2 px apart on average, against 4.8 px for A and B, whose fronts drift by up to 15 px). Its walls were 6.4 % apart, so it had the one allowed repair edit (even the lighting, change nothing else), which brought them to 0.3 % and its tops from 34 % to 11 % darker without moving anything (overlap 0.983). Rejected: A, whose walls were the flattest of the first three (3.6 %) but whose edges put painted pixels on the wrong faces of the normal map.

Observations

  • Is the painting flat-lit? Partly. Asked for even, shadowless light, the generator painted the big surfaces evenly: the first three candidates' two stone walls were 3.6–6.4 % apart, and one repair edit brought the chosen painting's to 0.3 %. It still paints form into the small parts. Tops, the ridge and the beams differ from the same material's sides by 8–25 %, so 1 of 7 materials are within ±7 % on every facing. The small groups swing by up to 18 points when the painting is moved 3 px, so their exact values are indicative. Today's painted Kitchen, for comparison, is 8.9 % apart between its walls and 13.8 % between its chimney faces.
  • Do the mirror pairs match? Relit, yes; baked, no. The stone walls facing screen right differ by 4.5 % between the relit original and its mirror. A true 3D mirror differs by 4.4 % for the same reason: the front wall carries more occlusion than the door wall. Baked, the mirror's screen-right wall has 50 % of the original's brightness. The mirror identity holds exactly: the largest difference is 0 of 255 under every sun.
  • A relit mirror is lit right but is still a different building. Its big roof slope faces the sun, so in the relit street every other roof glows orange. The true 3D render does the same (the sun section shows it). Mirroring through normals fixes the light, not the shape. Whether the alternating roofs read as variety or as noise is a call for the eye.
  • The sun-facing roof clips. In the relit mirror, 36.7 % of the building reaches 255 in a channel; in the true render's mirror, 42.2 %. The game's gamma-space sun brightens a sun-facing slope by about 1.9, against 1.33 for the sunlit wall. The earlier 3D look test's palette answered that by storing roofs at 1/1.6. A single K for every material cannot, so a relit roof would need its own K, or a darker roof paint.
  • Normals alone miss cast shadows. Relit in its own colour, the blockout differs from the true render by 11 of 255 on average, and 32.9 % of pixels differ by more than 16. The roof's shadow over the recess and the chimneys' shadows on the roof are what is missing. The occlusion term covers only the corners. A shadow term per sun, baked or from a proxy mesh, would be the missing part.
  • The painted detail survives the relight. Stone joints, tile lips, plank grain and copper stay legible at 63 points a unit. At the default zoom the relit street reads as the same kind of object as the baked one. The painted form on the tile lips reads as texture under every sun.
  • Style. Stepping moves the tones by a mean of 19 of 255, and mostly bands the curved props; each large face is one tone already. The detail relief is weak by design (a mean of 2.5) and shows only in the joints at the closest zoom.
  • Cost. Relit, a building is an albedo plus one packed data texture: about 0.90 MB at ASTC 6 × 6. A second, correctly lit baked sprite for the mirror would cost the same, but would cover one sun and one orientation. The relit pair covers every sun and both.
  • What the generator did wrong. It returned 1254-pixel canvases for a 1024 target, placed the building up to 18 px off until fitted, painted the gable window as blue glass instead of warm light in two of the three candidates (the chosen one among them), and topped the chimneys with pyramid caps, which the blockout's outline cuts off. After a scale-and-shift fit, the chosen painting's edges sit 2.3 px from the blockout's on average.
